result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked zebra crosswalk and wide sidewalks, though one side is currently impacted by construction fencing and barrels. The area is a high-activity commercial zone with transit access, but lacks visible dedicated pedestrian signals at the immediate crossing.

hazards.name: Construction Obstructions
hazards.description: Fencing and orange barrels narrow the pedestrian walkway and may force pedestrians closer to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street and near the crosswalk entrance on the left.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signal
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal head is visible to guide crossing timing at this marked crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install signals that show remaining crossing time to improve safety and predictability.

interventions.title: Improved Work Zone Channelization
interventions.description: Ensure construction barriers maintain a clear, wide, and accessible path for all pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is significantly compromised by active construction that has completely blocked the sidewalk on the left side of the street. While a marked crosswalk and traffic signals are present, the lack of a protected temporary walkway forces pedestrians into the roadway or requires them to cross the street unexpectedly.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Closure
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left side is entirely blocked by construction fencing, forcing pedestrians into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, extending from the foreground into the distance.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Construction barrels and fencing at the corner may obscure pedestrians from the view of turning motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground left corner near the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Temporary Pedestrian Bypass
interventions.description: Implement a protected, ADA-compliant temporary walkway using water-filled barriers to maintain pedestrian access during construction.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing transverse crosswalk markings to a high-visibility continental pattern to improve driver awareness.

result.summary: The image shows a standard urban intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, signals, and marked crosswalks. While functional, the environment lacks advanced safety features like high-visibility markings or curb extensions to shorten crossing distances.

hazards.name: Low-visibility crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The transverse (two-line) crosswalk markings are less visible to approaching motorists compared to high-visibility continental patterns.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground.

hazards.name: Wide intersection radius
hazards.description: The wide corners may encourage higher vehicle turning speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace existing transverse markings with continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide one-way urban street with a high-visibility zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. Pedestrian safety is compromised by significant sidewalk obstructions due to construction on the right and a lack of visible dedicated pedestrian signals.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Construction fencing and materials on the right side of the street significantly narrow the usable sidewalk space and may force pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Wide One-Way Roadway
hazards.description: The multi-lane one-way configuration can encourage higher vehicle speeds and increases the crossing distance for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, the main roadway.

interventions.title: Construction Zone Pedestrian Management
interventions.description: Ensure a continuous, ADA-compliant pedestrian path is maintained through or around the construction site with proper signage and protection.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear right-of-way information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.
